headline: Köln without three strikers, still narrow favourites
summary: Saturday's Bundesliga game in Cologne sets a wounded favourite against a side that struggles to create. Reports say Köln are without three senior strikers, and their best recent result was the 2-1 home derby against Gladbach. Schalke lost 0-1 at home to Mainz last weekend and average only 0.90 expected goals a game; Edin Džeko is doubtful, according to Sportschau. Even so, the market makes Köln 47.4% favourites, with the bookmaker's margin removed — under half. In goals, the market rates them only 0.4 the better side, and the goal line sits at 3.0, with over and under level.
read: Köln are narrow home favourites at 47.4% against a Schalke side without a win in three, and both teams are short of a recognised centre-forward. The market expects about three goals and rates Köln just under half a goal the better side — a tight game between two teams in the bottom half of the table.

facts.fact: Köln are the favourites at 47.4% — under half the chance, with the draw and Schalke splitting the rest.
facts.meaning: The market sees a tight home win, not a mismatch: Köln are the side to back but by a narrow margin.

facts.fact: Köln are reported to be without all three senior centre-forwards — Dallinga, Ache and Rondic — through injury, though there is new hope over Ache.
facts.meaning: The favourites may have to improvise up front, which is a big part of why their price is only just the right side of even money.

facts.fact: Schalke have taken one point from their last three Bundesliga games (LLD).
facts.meaning: They come to Cologne on a downward run, which is the form line behind Köln's favouritism.

facts.fact: Schalke average only 0.90 expected goals per game this season.
facts.meaning: They create very little — the weaker attacking output of the two sides by a wide margin.

facts.fact: On the handicap the market rates Köln about 0.4 goals the better side, with the main line at -0.5.
The market's goal line sits at 3.0, with over and under both priced at 50%.
facts.meaning: Three goals is the expected total — the market is pricing an open game rather than a grind.

facts.fact: Köln have won once in their last five (LWLDL), and that win was the 2-1 home derby against Gladbach.
facts.meaning: Köln's favouritism rests on home advantage and Schalke's slump more than on their own results.

facts.fact: Schalke have 5 points from six games in their first season back in the Bundesliga.
facts.meaning: A promoted side already in the bottom four — the trip to Köln is a pressure game, not a free hit.

sources.fact: Köln lost 1-0 away at Eintracht Frankfurt last matchday after a 2-1 derby win over Gladbach the week before.
Köln are without strikers Thijs Dallinga and Ragnar Ache through injury, leaving them short of a centre-forward.
BILD reports a surprise guest at Köln's secret training, raising the possibility of a returning FC star being available against Schalke.
Defensive midfielder Joel Schmied is out for Köln, while there is new hope regarding Ragnar Ache ahead of the home game against Schalke.
Köln legend Pierre Littbarski says the club has 'too much mediocrity' and discusses coach René Wagner in a BILD interview.
With Dallinga, Ache and Imad Rondic injured, Malek El Mala could be in Köln's Bundesliga squad against Schalke for the first time, potentially forming an El-Mala double.
Schalke are three games without a win and are looking to stop their downward trend in Cologne.
Schalke were newly promoted and took five points from their opening five Bundesliga matches, but suffered a frustrating 2-1 defeat to league leaders Freiburg.
